result:
I re-ran the full DG3 review on the repaired candidate, and my verdict is **PASS**. F-DG3-180 is verified **CLOSED_VERIFIED** and I raised no new findings. Two test runs exited non-zero by design (one flaky unit test, one strict layout probe of mine); both are explained below.

The candidate is `sha256:f2b4c77a…` (757 files, source `ce988e2`). The ID recomputed identically at the start, in my disposable clone and at the end. HEAD moved during my run, but only files under `docs/delivery/` changed.

**F-DG3-180 (the inherited-approval badge overflow)**
- **My round-2 probe:** unchanged, it now passes in English and Arabic under both locale settings. All 7 of 7 badges sit inside their gate card or field; in round 2, 7 of 7 (English) and 4 of 7 (Arabic) were outside.
- **New probe for the gaps:** it covers all five badge states at nine widths from 320 to 1920 px, plus 200% text at 1280 and 390 px. In every measurement the badge stays inside its card, wraps, isn't clipped and overlaps nothing. The fix is scoped: every other status chip still doesn't wrap.
- **One state still scrolls sideways:** 390 px with 200% text. This is not the badge. The gate grid's 18rem minimum card width, unchanged since DG2, makes each card wider than the screen. The clause stays inside its card and can be reached by scrolling. That state is below the 320 px width WCAG requires to reflow, and WCAG allows scrolling when text is enlarged, so I recorded it as an observation, not a finding. It's why this new probe exits non-zero.

**Full regression**
- **Static checks:** typecheck, build, lint, OpenAPI lint (270 operations), the no-CDN check, formatting and contrast all exit 0.
- **Formula guard (the T-DG3-KBE-E repair):**
  - A throwaway file with 15 forbidden code patterns is refused (25 errors).
  - I injected a run-time-assembled `constructor` key, which lint can't see, by design. The new code-generation-disabled test project caught it with 25 EvalError failures, and `pnpm test` failed.
  - The formula acceptance results are unchanged (3.30 → 57.5, 100000 SAR, 151852.11 SAR).
- **Unit tests:** on Node 22 and 24, with the locale unset and with C.UTF-8, both test invocations pass (1587 tests, then 190).
  - One run, Node 22 with the locale unset, failed once. A DG2 sign-out test hit its 1-second wait while the machine was heavily loaded by the other reviewers.
  - The failure dump showed user B's own page with no data from user A. The rerun passed and 8 repeats of that test all passed, so I classed it as a timing flake.
- **Integration:** two runs on disposable PostgreSQL, 793/793 each; all 27 migrations apply and every pending-operations list is empty.
- **Browser tests:** the product journeys pass 182/182 per locale setting. The +10 versus round 2 is the new inherited-approval spec. All 32 requirements pass literally: 163 checks per language, 0 failed, with axe reporting 0 violations and the auditor user read-only throughout.
- **Validators:** register, pipeline, and DG2/DG1 historical all pass.

Two other failures in my evidence were my own test mistakes, kept as trial logs:
- My first lint probe used an ESLint output format that ESLint 10 no longer ships.
- My first 200%-text attempt was blocked by the app's Content Security Policy. That is the policy working correctly; I switched to a method it allows.

Live registry, live CI and Keycloak are recorded as offline residuals, as the assignment specified.

**Disclosure:** after all my results were in, the git log showed commit messages saying the code-security reviewer found F-DG3-100 still not fixed. That finding isn't mine to verify, and it changed nothing in my results.

Files are in `docs/delivery/reviews/DG3/round-3/`:
- `qa-verifier.json`
- `qa-verifier.verifications.json`
- `qa-verifier.md`

The evidence is under `docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG3/qa/round-3/`, with every non-zero exit explained in `RUN-NOTES.md`. My test spec is `docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG3/qa/tests/round-3/e2e/dg3-qa-r3.spec.ts`.
